record.original_question: What necessary and sufficient conditions guarantee the existence of bi-orthogonal local coordinate systems on a Riemannian manifold, without assuming any affine connections a priori?

evidence.quote: Give a necessary and sufficient condition for bi-coordinates to exist on a Riemannian manifold (cf. [25, §19]).

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $(M,g)$ be a smooth Riemannian manifold of dimension $n$. A pair of local coordinate systems $(\theta^1,\dots,\theta^n)$ and $(\eta_1,\dots,\eta_n)$ defined on a common open set $U\subset M$ is called a system of bi-orthogonal (or "bi-") coordinates if the corresponding coordinate vector fields are bi-orthogonal with respect to $g$, i.e.
$$g\!\left(\frac{\partial}{\partial \theta^{i}},\frac{\partial}{\partial \eta_{j}}\right) \;=\; \delta_{i}^{\,j} \qquad \text{on } U,\ \text{for all } i,j\in\{1,\dots,n\}.$$
No affine connection on $M$ is assumed in advance; only the Riemannian metric $g$ is given.

Determine necessary and sufficient conditions on $(M,g)$ (or, locally, on $g$ in a neighbourhood of a point $p\in M$) under which such a pair of bi-orthogonal local coordinate systems exists around $p$.
artifact.status_search_result: Web searches surface closely related results (existence of orthogonal coordinates on Riemannian manifolds is automatic in dimension ≤3 but fails generically in higher dimensions; dual/affine coordinate systems exist on dually flat spaces in information geometry), but no source was found that gives a complete necessary-and-sufficient characterization for the existence of bi-orthogonal coordinates on a general Riemannian manifold without presupposing an affine connection. The status of this precise question could not be verified.

status_evidence.title: Non-existence of orthogonal coordinates on the complex and quaternionic projective spaces
status_evidence.snippet: Existence of orthogonal coordinates on Riemannian manifolds of dimension > 3 is overdetermined and does not hold generically.
status_evidence.claim: Related orthogonal-coordinate existence problems are known to be obstructed in dimensions greater than 3.

status_evidence.title: Dual Connections (Mini-course in Information Geometry)
status_evidence.snippet: On a dually flat space, two affine coordinate systems exist that are biorthogonal with respect to the metric and related by a Legendre transformation.
status_evidence.claim: Bi-orthogonal (dual) coordinate systems exist when the manifold carries a dually flat structure, but this presupposes a pair of affine connections.
